name: Question 12
problem: Given the ellipsoid $\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{10}+{y}^{2}+\frac{(z+1)^{2}}{5}=1$, find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
worked_solution:
From the ellipsoid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{10}+{y}^{2}+\frac{(z+1)^{2}}{5} & =1 \\ (z+1)^{2} & =5(1-\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{10}-{y}^{2}) \\ z+1 & =\pm \sqrt{5(1-\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{10}-{y}^{2})}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}1-\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{10}-{y}^{2}\ge 0 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{10}+{y}^{2}\le 1\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the interior of the ellipse $\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{10}+{y}^{2}=1$ and its boundary. 

Therefore, the domain is 

$$
{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{10}+{y}^{2}\le 1}.
$$

Question 12
?

Given the ellipsoid (x−2)210+y2+(z+1)25=1, find the domain of z=z(x,y).

a
{(x,y):(x−1)25+(y−2)210>1}
b
{(x,y):(x−2)2+y210<1}
c
{(x,y):(x−1)25+(y−2)210<1}
d
{(x,y):(x−2)210+y2≤1}
e
{(x,y):(x−2)2+(y−2)210<1}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

From the ellipsoid equation, we make z the subject as follows:

(x−2)210+y2+(z+1)25=1(z+1)2=5(1−(x−2)210−y2)z+1=±5(1−(x−2)210−y2)

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have:

1−(x−2)210−y2≥0(x−2)210+y2≤1

which gives the interior of the ellipse (x−2)210+y2=1 and its boundary.

Therefore, the domain is {(x,y):(x−2)210+y2≤1}.
